name: Slopcore Music Video
tagline: A song full of a scene's in-jokes goes in, a music video with one star, every lyric on screen and a graphic explaining every line comes out.
description: A lyric music video made the way anabology and Claude made ESCAPE VELOCITY, CLODYSSEY and BLISS: one photographic lead (Claudia, the open character, or your own) in Midjourney plates, Seedance shots with lip sync measured from the song, and motion design drawn in code over it: every sung word on screen at its time, a graphic that explains each line, and a countdown or counter that escalates to the end. Made for songs about a scene's memes, like the AI timeline.
bring: A topic with its own slang (the AI timeline works great), or the story you want
A song, or lyrics we write together and make in Suno
Optional: your own lead instead of Claudia, a look, an accent colour
A budget for images and video (from about $20 to $250)
get: A 16:9 music video as long as the song (2:30–5 min), every sung word on screen at its time

needs.name: Hyperframes, or your project's video tool
Midjourney for the plates
examples: an image API on the Quick scale

needs.name: Suno, unless you bring a song
The Claudia gallery (her canon, every prompt the films ran)

examples.label: Not Available in Your Region
examples.note: A second film made with this method: Europe's launch day of its own frontier model, told as a perfect-day schedule with a flip-clock spine that runs to 17:00, when the model clocks out by law and the screen says 'Not available in your region'. A generated lead (not Claudia) in API image models instead of Midjourney, Seedance for the sung shots, a French-house Suno song, and a graphic on every line.

steps: Pick the story and make the song; you pick the take by ear
Time every word and beat, and test the lead's face on four plates
Board every shot with its graphic, then review the board and the cost before anything is spent
Make the plates and the moving shots, with lip sync measured from the song
Draw the lyrics, graphics and the countdown in code, and review each version in FrameJam
